solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Club offering card on initiation of members (4)

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece sitting on another follows it
the initiation of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: an ace is a playing card

annotation.surface: A golf or social club is advertising a playing card to new members at their initiation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a society or a suit of cards; it is the weapon, a mace.
annotation.definitionFit: A mace is a heavy spiked club used as a weapon.

clue.text: Deranged, idles on wagon (10)

blocks.note: to moon about is to idle
a truck is a goods wagon

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits on top of the next

annotation.surface: Someone lazing about on a cart seems to have lost their mind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On wagon' tempts you to think of being on the wagon, off drink; here wagon is simply TRUCK.
annotation.definitionFit: Moonstruck once meant driven mad by the moon, hence deranged.

clue.text: Bolshevik after money, focused (7)

indicators.note: the Bolshevik comes after the money

annotation.surface: A revolutionary, bent on getting money, is single-minded about it.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sets Bolshevik after money as a motive; in the wordplay 'after' is just position.
annotation.definitionFit: Centred and focused both mean concentrated on one point.

clue.text: A card game that’s driven by force? (5,5)

blocks.note: a trick-taking game, like hearts, in which the queen of spades is the card to avoid
force here is the police force, and what they drive is a van for prisoners

annotation.surface: A card game so rough it seems to be played under compulsion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Force' reads as compulsion; it is the police force, whose prisoner van is the Black Maria, also the name of the card game.
annotation.definitionFit: Black Maria names both a card game like hearts and the police van for prisoners.

clue.text: Good hearts in reality broken a good, good way (5-4)

indicators.note: the letters are broken up and reassembled

blocks.note: H is hearts in card notation

annotation.surface: Kind hearts, when reality shatters them, find a good way through.
annotation.walkthrough: The repeated 'good' is the definition's emphasis: a good, good way is a very long way indeed.
annotation.definitionFit: A light-year is the distance light travels in a year, an enormous way.

clue.text: Reach to grab last of Roquefort, French cheese (5)

indicators.note: COME grabs the T and holds it inside
the last letter of the word

blocks.note: to come to a place is to reach it

annotation.surface: Someone stretches for the last of the Roquefort on the French cheeseboard.
annotation.walkthrough: Roquefort is a French cheese too, which makes it look like the definition; it only supplies T.
annotation.definitionFit: Comté is a hard cheese from the Jura region of France.

clue.text: Double-edged sword evidently sparkling, sabre originally encased in assortment of flashy jewels? (5,8)

indicators.note: take the original, first, letters of the words
to be encased in something is to be enclosed by it, so ESS sits inside BLING

blocks.note: an assortment is a mixed selection
first letters of evidently, sparkling, sabre

annotation.surface: A sparkling sabre set in a pile of glittering jewels, as ornamental as it is dangerous.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sword' and 'sabre' keep you in the armoury; the definition is the idiom for something with good and bad sides.
annotation.definitionFit: A double-edged sword is a thing with both benefits and drawbacks, a mixed blessing.

clue.text: Place in orchestral part for broadcast (7)

indicators.note: a thing placed in another is held inside it, so LAY sits inside REED

blocks.note: the reeds are a section of the orchestra

annotation.surface: A radio station finds a slot for an orchestral piece in its schedule.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Orchestral part' suggests a score or a passage of music; here it is a section of players, the reeds.
annotation.definitionFit: A relayed programme is one broadcast, passed on to listeners.

clue.text: In Malay, a housemaid (4)

indicators.note: the answer is sitting in the words that follow

annotation.surface: A phrasebook note giving the Malay word for a domestic servant.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a translation, and the Asian setting fits the answer, but the word is hidden across the gap.
annotation.definitionFit: An ayah is a nursemaid or maidservant in South Asia and former British colonies.

clue.text: Old man’s bandaged up in a series of grunts (7)

indicators.note: O and KING wrap around IN like a bandage

blocks.note: a king is a chess man

annotation.surface: An injured old man, strapped up, can only grunt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like part of the phrase 'bandaged up in'; it is the very letters being wrapped.
annotation.definitionFit: Oinking is the grunting noise a pig makes, kept up in a series.

clue.text: White lies? Seemingly not! (2,4,7)

blocks.note: the surface reading is harmless social fibs; the setter's reading is white wine, where lies might be found
the reply denies it: a Latin proverb holds that wine brings out the truth, not lies

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether small social fibs count, and is told they do not.
annotation.walkthrough: White lies are harmless fibs; read White as white wine, and the Latin proverb says there is truth, not lies, in wine.
annotation.definitionFit: In vino veritas is Latin for 'in wine, truth': drink loosens tongues.

clue.text: Greatest area around funny bone (7)

indicators.note: to go around something is to enclose it, so MAX and A surround ILL

annotation.surface: Someone looks for the biggest region of the funny bone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Funny bone' reads as one phrase; split it, and funny is ILL while bone alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the maxilla, the upper jaw, is one particular bone of the skull.

clue.text: Feeding time, Thursday Eve so dissimilar? (6,7)

indicators.note: the letters are made into something different

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether Thursday evening is really so different as a time to eat.
annotation.walkthrough: The wordplay offers one day of the week and the answer is another. Shrove Tuesday, before Lent, is Pancake Day, when the larder is used up in a feast.
annotation.definitionFit: Shrove Tuesday is the day of feasting on pancakes before the Lenten fast.

clue.text: Biting insect circling chain on bike, finally (10)

indicators.note: to circle something is to ring it, so ANT surrounds STRING and E
'finally' points to where a word ends, its last letter

blocks.note: a string of beads is a chain

annotation.surface: A stinging insect buzzes round a bicycle chain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Biting insect' reads as one phrase; the definition is Biting alone, in the sense of sharp or severe.
annotation.definitionFit: Astringent criticism is biting: sharp and severe.

clue.text: Gas lit behind unit for a physicist (5)

indicators.note: what is behind another comes after it, so ON follows RAD

blocks.note: the rad is a unit of absorbed radiation

annotation.surface: A physicist lights a gas burner at the back of the lab.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gas lit' suggests gaslight; lit is ON, and gas alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: radon is one of the noble gases, heavy and radioactive.

clue.text: Rearrange final seed drills from end to end (9)

indicators.note: put the letters in a new order

annotation.surface: A gardener is told to re-sow the last seed drills along the whole row.
annotation.walkthrough: Seed drills are furrows for sowing; the definition's drills means bores through, as gunfire along a line does.
annotation.definitionFit: To enfilade is to rake a line of troops with fire from end to end.

clue.text: Number of vessels filled with melted ices, most soft (9)

indicators.note: FLEET is filled with the other letters
melted ice loses its shape, so the letters of ICES lose their order

blocks.note: a fleet is a number of ships

annotation.surface: A number of dishes filled with ice cream that has gone soft.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' suggests bowls, which suits melted ices; they are ships, a FLEET.
annotation.definitionFit: Fleeciest means most like fleece, the softest.

clue.text: Country always extremely desperate, put a lid on that! (4,5)

indicators.note: take the extreme, outer, letters

blocks.note: to cap is to put a lid on

annotation.surface: A country always on the edge is told to calm down and keep quiet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put a lid on that!' is the idiom for stop it; in the wordplay the lid, CAP, goes on top of the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: Cape Verde is an island country off West Africa.

clue.text: Noodle in quantity of butter with a sauce (7)

indicators.note: a thing put in another is held inside it, so ASS sits inside PAT
'with' means accompanied by, so A is added alongside

blocks.note: a noodle is a fool, an ass

annotation.surface: A recipe: toss the noodles in a knob of butter and some sauce.
annotation.walkthrough: In a kitchen surface 'noodle' is pasta; it is the slang for a fool.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: passata, sieved tomatoes, is a sauce base in Italian cooking.

clue.text: Journey beyond southern river (5)

indicators.note: what lies beyond another comes after it, so TOUR follows S

annotation.surface: A trip taking in a river in the south.
annotation.walkthrough: The Stour is the name of several English rivers, among them the one in Constable country.
annotation.definitionFit: The Stour is a river, indeed several in England.

clue.text: Source of oval fruit, case of timber in that? (3,4)

definitions.text: Source of oval fruit, case of timber in that?

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter
the case of a word is its outside letters
a thing placed in another is held inside it, so TR sits inside AKEE

blocks.note: the akee, or ackee, is a tropical fruit

annotation.surface: What produces egg-shaped fruit, with timber hidden inside it?
annotation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes the tree: its oval fruit is the acorn and its wood is timber. 'That' points to the fruit the case of timber goes into.
annotation.definitionFit: An oak tree bears oval acorns and yields timber.

clue.text: Bound to get scared, youth (6,7)

annotation.surface: A youngster is sure to take fright.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' looks like 'certain to'; bound is a leap, SPRING.
annotation.definitionFit: A spring chicken is a young person, as in 'no spring chicken'.

clue.text: Firstly, North ably redistributes cards, our dealer (5)

indicators.note: take the first letter of each word

blocks.note: first letters of North, ably, redistributes, cards, our

annotation.surface: At the bridge table, North deftly reshuffles and deals the cards.
annotation.walkthrough: The bridge setting makes 'dealer' the one who deals cards; it is a drug dealer. North is a bridge seat, and 'redistributes' looks like an anagram signal but only lends its R.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang: narco, short for narcotics trafficker, names a drug dealer rather than a card dealer.

clue.text: Jumper, possibly, back on top of girl (4)

indicators.note: in a down clue, FRO sits on top of G
the top of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: to and fro: fro means back

annotation.surface: A sweater, maybe, draped over the shoulders of a girl.
annotation.walkthrough: A jumper is a British sweater, which fits the girl; here it is anything that jumps, and 'possibly' flags the frog as one example.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example, flagged by 'possibly': the frog is one creature that gets about by leaping.

clue.text: Table bearing a fowl (7)

indicators.note: ROSTER carries A inside it

blocks.note: a roster is a table of duties

annotation.surface: A dinner table carrying a bird.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface lays a bird on a dining table; the table is a rota, ROSTER.
annotation.definitionFit: A roaster is a chicken or other fowl suitable for roasting.

clue.text: English are besieging capital in Dakar — defend yourself! (2,5)

indicators.note: a besieging army surrounds its target, so ARE surrounds D
the capital, first, letter of Dakar

annotation.surface: The English are laying siege to the capital of Senegal, and its defenders are called to arms.
annotation.walkthrough: Dakar really is a capital, of Senegal, which is the misdirection; 'capital' means its capital letter, D.
annotation.definitionFit: En garde is the fencer's call to take a defensive position.

clue.text: Dope cheers for ordinary folk (5,5)

blocks.note: grass is slang for cannabis, dope
to root for a team is to cheer it

annotation.surface: A stoner raises a glass to the common people.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' reads as a toast; it is the verb, roots, as in rooting for a team.
annotation.definitionFit: The grassroots are the ordinary members of a party or movement.

clue.text: Discarded Franglais newspaper? (4)

blocks.note: the FT is the Financial Times

annotation.surface: A newspaper written in mixed French and English has been thrown away.
annotation.walkthrough: Franglais mixes French and English, and so does the wordplay: French LE plus the English FT, the Financial Times.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what has been left, like a coat on a train, has been cast off or discarded.
